fixes.explanation: Those sound like places with plenty of people, but they aren't the ones Jesus names. He says the hypocrites love to pray “…standing in the synagogues and on the street corners to be seen by men.” (Matthew 6:5) Wells and city squares are fair guesses, friend. The two places to hold onto are the synagogues and the street corners.

Gifts came up earlier in the passage, friend, when Jesus talked about giving to the needy. But this verse is about prayer. Jesus says the pagans “…think that by their many words they will be heard.” (Matthew 6:7) The word that fits the blank is “words.”

Jesus says the opposite, friend. “But if you do not forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive yours.” (Matthew 6:15) It's a serious line, and He says it plainly. That makes this statement false.

The temple isn't part of this verse, friend. Jesus says to anoint your head and wash your face “…so that your fasting will not be obvious to men, but only to your Father, who is unseen.” (Matthew 6:17-18) The reason He gives is about who gets to see it.

Double sounds great, friend, but that's not what Jesus says. If you do your righteous acts to be seen by men, “…you will have no reward from your Father in heaven.” (Matthew 6:1) No reward at all, so there's nothing there to double.

Smaller is a reasonable guess, friend, but that's not what Jesus says. He says if you do your righteous acts to be seen by men, “…you will have no reward from your Father in heaven.” (Matthew 6:1) It isn't a little reward or a shrunken one. It's none.

The temple isn't the place Jesus names here, friend. He says to “…go into your inner room, shut your door, and pray to your Father, who is unseen.” (Matthew 6:6) Picture it: door shut, nobody watching, just you and your Father.

Words is the first one. Jesus says the pagans “…think that by their many words they will be heard.” (Matthew 6:7) Their thinking is that more words means being heard. Jesus tells His listeners not to be like them (Matthew 6:8).

Not quite, friend. The prayer says, “Your kingdom come, Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.” (Matthew 6:10) Earth is right there in the request. It asks for God's will to be done on earth as it is in heaven.

Enemies are a natural guess, friend, but they aren't named in this verse. The prayer says, “And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.” (Matthew 6:13) The evil one is the one it names.

Priests aren't in this verse, friend. Jesus says the hypocrites “…disfigure their faces to show men they are fasting.” (Matthew 6:16) The audience He names is just “men.” That's the word for the blank.

Right. Jesus says, “But when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face…” (Matthew 6:17) It's the opposite of the hypocrites disfiguring their faces. The purpose He gives is “…so that your fasting will not be obvious to men…” (Matthew 6:18)
